title: The Bell That Only Rang for Krishna

source.name: Traditional Krishna/Vrindavan story
source.episode_or_reference: Story idea supplied in stories/story_ideas.md; traditional account/folklore treatment, not presented as a direct scripture quotation.

characters.description: Warm Indian grandfather in his late 60s, white kurta-pajama, simple shawl, expressive kind face.
Indian boy aged about 10 in simple Indian clothes, curious expressive face.
Indian girl aged about 8 in simple Indian clothes, curious expressive face.
Mother Yashoda in traditional Vrindavan sari and jewelry, warm expressive face.

Bal Krishna, approximately 6–8 years old, unmistakably Shyam-varna with deep rich blue skin clearly visible across face, neck, arms and hands; slim small pre-adolescent child proportions, never fat, chubby, muscular, adult or teenager. Soft round childlike face, large expressive dark eyes, short dark curly hair, one single peacock feather centered in his crown, yellow pitambar and simple traditional gold jewelry. Fixed identity: Krishna alone is blue and Krishna alone wears the single peacock feather.

locations.description: Peaceful Vrindavan village courtyard beneath a huge old banyan tree, exposed roots, soft afternoon light, earthen ground, clay pots, village greenery and a calm storytelling atmosphere.
Gokul butter room with a clay pot hanging from a wooden beam and a small bell tied above it.

supporting_assets.description: Small-to-medium traditional round earthen Gokul matka, suspended low from a roof/ceiling wooden beam by a visible rope, approximately just above a child's reach; no legs, no feet, never sitting on the floor. The open pot contains fresh white hand-churned Indian makkhan formed as several small rounded soft balls/laddooos, irregularly round and soft, never a cube, slab, stick or yellow Western butter. Exactly one small brass bell is attached beneath the same pot; no second bell.

dialogue.speaker: grandfather
dialogue.text: आज की कहानी में एक छोटी-सी घंटी है… और वह सिर्फ कन्हैया की वजह से बजती थी!

dialogue.speaker: grandfather
dialogue.text: घंटी ने जैसे कहा—‘कन्हैया, जब आपका भोग लगेगा, तो मैं कैसे न बजूँ?’

dialogue.speaker: grandfather
dialogue.text: कहानी हमें याद दिलाती है कि प्रेम से किया गया भोग भगवान से जुड़ने का माध्यम माना जाता है।
